feature: Picking a title never resizes the picture
summary: Picking a title, a part of it, or keying a value no longer grows the timeline, so the picture above keeps its size and the panel stays put. The rows a pick opens scroll inside the timeline, and a lane that opens below its foot is scrolled into view.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the sample recording with the timeline open.

try.do: Right-click the V1 track header and choose Add Track Above, then right-click V2 and choose Add Title Page > Stacked Stagger.
Press Command-Return to finish the headline. Its rows (Title, Opacity, Position) open on the timeline and the picture does not move.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Escape. The headline's rows fold and the picture stays the same size.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Escape again, then click the headline on the canvas to pick it again.
Scroll with the wheel over the timeline to bring V1 and its sound back into view.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: With the headline picked, use Animate a property > Color. The Color lane opens under the clip and the timeline scrolls just enough to show it.

evaluate: Does the picture now hold still when you pick a title, a part of it, or press Escape?
With a title's headline picked, is losing sight of V1 below the timeline's foot acceptable, given a scroll or a drag of the divider brings it back?
When you key a new value and its lane opens below the visible tracks, does the small scroll that brings it in feel right, or would you rather it stayed put?
Would you want the timeline a little taller by default now that it no longer grows on its own?
rough: This builds option b on the open card about keying a property (clicking-a-cut-keying-a-value-and-undoing-it-ans-when-you-key-a-property-on-a-vid). If you answer a there, this task's behaviour follows your answer instead.
The cost of option b is visible: picking a title's headline on the sample opens three rows, and V1 slides to the timeline's foot with its sound below it, until you scroll or drag the divider up.
No mock covers how the timeline's height reacts to a pick; the mock only caps the dock's height.
Folding a track group and opening a captions track's words still change the timeline's height, because those are commands on the tracks themselves, not picks.

The Library-only height hold from double-clicking-a-library-title-tile-inserts-it is gone: the general rule covers it, and title-presets-library-shelf-walk still double-clicks Keynote Clean by the pointer and lands it.
